SPECIFICATION FOR 
PEDIGREE HATCHING BOXES FOR POULTRY 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope — This standard prescribes the material construction and other datails of pedigree hatching 
boxes for pouitry. 

2. Terminology — For the purpose of this standard, the following definition shall apply. 

2.1 Pedigree Hatching Box — A box for keeping eggs of individual hen or a group of hens mated to a 
particular male for hatching in the incubator for maintaining pedigree record as per the dam and/or 
the sire. 

3. Types 

3.0 The hatching box shall be of the following types. 

3.1 Type A — Box without partitions ( see Fig. 1 ). 




All dimensions in millimetres.

4. Material 

4.1 Box and Partitions — Galvanized steel sheet [ see IS : 277-1985 Specification for galvanized steel 
sheets ( plain and corrugated ) ( fourth revision ) ], aluminium sheets [ see IS *. 737-1974 'Specification 
for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloys, sheet and strip (for general engineering purposes) 
( second rew5/o/7 )], aluminium angle section [ 5ee IS : 3908-1986 Specification for aluminium equal 
leg angles ( first revision ) ], and mild steel wire [ see IS : 280-1978 'Specification for mild steel wire 
for general engineering purposes ( third revision ) ] which shall be galvanized. 

4.2 Lid, Hinges and Locking Device — GaWan'ued stee\ sheet [see 15:277-1985, aluminium sheets 
( see IS : 737-1974 ) and wire mesh [ see IS : 4948-1974 Specification for welded steel wire fabric for 
general use ( first revision) ]. 

5. Construction 

5.1 The galvanized steel sheet and aluminium sheet for box should be of 0'63 and 10 mm minimum 
thickness, respectively and for lid 1*0 and 1*25 mm, respectively. The thickness of wire of wire-netting 
should be 056 mm. Wire netting may be tin jointed or rivetted to sheet or angle section. 

5.2 In case of Type A, the lid may be held in position with the help of locking system. 

5.3 In case of Type B, small end ot the lid should have a lip turned downwards while the other end 
should be straight for smooth sliding of the lid over the box. The partition may slide on four wires 
which pass through the partition and also hold them in position. 

6. Dimensions — The dimensions of hatching boxes of Type A and Type B shall as far as possible be, 
as given in Fig. 1 and 2 respectively. 

7. Finish — The finish of the boxes shall be smooth so that delicate newly born chicks are not injured. 
All the joints shall be finished smooth and properly secured. 

B. Marking and Packing 

8.1 /l/far/://?5f— Each hatching box shall carry the following particulars on name plate affixed on one 
side of the box: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, 

b) Type of the box, and 

c) Capacity ( number of eggs ) of the box. 



IS : 7517 - 1987 

8.1,1 Standard Mark — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

8.2 Packing — The hatching boxes may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier. 

9. Sampling — Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the sampling plan 
and criteria for conformity shall be as given in Appendix A of IS ; 6228-1971 'Specification for poultry 
egg fertility tester'. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

For keeping an accurate record of individual hatching results and for maintaining the pedigree of the 
chicks, it Is necessary to have eggs from individual hen placed in separate pedigree cages during 
incubation. The eggs of each bird are kept in cages along with their details. These are then 
kept in hatchers for hatching after 18 days of incubation. 

This standard covering the details of pedigree hatching boxes was first published in 1974. Based on 
the comments received from Central Avian Research Institute ( ICAR ), Izatnagar, the standard has been 
revised to make it up to date.
